portInfo.description: Cartagena’s harbour faces a compact city with Carthaginian, Roman, naval and Modernist layers. Instead of spending a short call on a regional coach tour, you can move between underwater archaeology, the Roman theatre and the old town with relatively little travel. Concepción Castle sits uphill; the harbour museums and lower streets are the gentler alternative.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: ARQUA — National Museum of Underwater Archaeology, Paseo Alfonso XII22, Cartagena: A maritime-history stop beside the port, focused on underwater finds rather than a generic city museum. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Check opening day and ticket rules.

Roman Theatre Museum, Roman Theatre Museum, behind Plaza del Ayuntamiento, Cartagena: The principal Roman-era visit, with a defined museum/site route. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Timed admission or queues can alter the day; do not enter the ruined cathedral independently.

Calle Mayor and Town Hall square, Calle Mayor/Plaza del Ayuntamiento, Cartagena: Read the Modernist façades on a flexible outdoor walk. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Individual buildings may not be open to visitors.

Concepción Castle and Torres Park, Castillo de la Concepción, Parque Torres, Cartagena: A hilltop historical viewpoint over the harbour. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Uphill access and any lift availability need checking.

Roman Forum quarter, Barrio del Foro Romano, El Molinete, Cartagena: A separate Roman urban-life visit that complements the theatre. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Do not equate nearby ruins with unrestricted public entry.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: ARQUA, the Roman theatre and the naval museum are separate institutions. Confirm which ticket you have, and preserve a flat waterfront alternative if the castle climb or its lift arrangements are unsuitable.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Terminal de Cruceros — dedicated cruise quay — Dársena de Cartagena,beside Club de Regatas,outside Puerto Deportivo
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The authority places the dedicated terminal beside the Club de Regatas, outside the yacht marina. Allow 20–30 minutes from the assigned gangway through the passenger exit to the waterfront, and another 10–20 minutes to the theatre/old town depending on route. These are editorial walking/clearance budgets. Official sources give different 200 m/500 m city-centre distances with unspecified endpoints; neither is a universal gangway-to-attraction route. Ask about any waterfront works and keep the assigned return gate. Murcia is a separate road excursion, not the port’s immediate city centre.
